0.long_answer: Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD) is a mental disorder characterized by a marked fear or anxiety about social situations, where an individual is exposed to possible scrutiny by others. It is often associated with body dysmorphic disorder (BDD), partly because both disorders involve significant social distress and avoidance behaviors. Research indicates that mental disorders frequently co-occur, with around 66% of cases involving one or more additional mental disorders. SAD, in particular, shares features with BDD as both conditions involve excessive self-consciousness and concern about negative evaluation in social contexts.
